posthoc_source_reason: The manufacturer-responsibility provision in Exhibit D.7 is redacted; the NPI definition alone does not establish the full duty.
“Swapping: blocked” does not distinguish legal prohibition from a temporary lack of liquidity.
Seller Party excludes Acquired Companies, ruling out author option C; stored B omits the employee-creation condition.
The contract says the provider may remove objectionable material; every option says it must remove the video.
Burst means high damage in a short interval; A paraphrases this function. Repeated option letters are a minor format flaw.
Fill means allowing specialists to pick first and covering the remaining role, supporting B.
Fines are Losses, and allocation depends on specific reimbursement and breach clauses; the generic scenario is not uniquely resolved by the overhead-cost sentence.
Stored A is contradicted by the express grant of rights to Documentation, including user and technical manuals; no safe replacement key is established.
The source-specific post-fix reindex rule is not linked to the question’s generic data-source approval.
All listed testnets are API-accessible but only two are web-accessible; the source does not impose the stated SDK test checklist.
Varnok is the second sign-off for a limit increase, supporting stored option B rather than model maintenance.
The source mentions native interoperability but no required chain-to-chain protocol endpoint.
The source describes onchain AMM liquidity and protocol-router execution, supporting A.
“Handled” does not specify a payment confirmation versus completion of an execution order.
Options A and D both describe rules of the SEC, which the contract calls the Commission.
Standard is a restricted deck format; a no-longer-legal card may require replacement in that queue.
The source identifies a self-custodial cryptocurrency wallet, supporting a separately controlled demo account.
The retained source does not state the fleet workflow following “Detail completed.”
The options contain only the literal letters A, B, C, and D.
Moshet is a scheduled venue-maintenance window.
The glossary identifies an external counterparty trading under approved credit.
Farm means repeating a game activity, supporting the core of A; its extra trade-item endpoint is not directly sourced.
The Multi-party Contract definition requires both named business groups to benefit from the third party; number of signatories is not the test.
The supplied documents do not describe the stated smart-vault patch or authorized upgrade.
The complete notice clause applies to facsimile notices on the next Business Day, absent earlier oral or written confirmation.
“Swapping unavailable” does not distinguish unsupported-token prohibition from temporary unavailability.
The source defines collateral but not clearance or an account-decommissioning test.
